problem_type: A budget enforced only between turns is not a per-request bound: inside one turn every step re-sends all earlier tool results, so input grows without limit
symptom: Long Agent conversations (read the script, write it back, repeat) send 88K to 146K input tokens in a single model request although the lane's registered budget is 80K; one turn costs 750K tokens in total, and real users hit 'Assistant request exceeded the context window'.
direct_cause: pi compacts only after a turn when the measured context is over the threshold; within a turn the lane's transform_context hook returned only a system prompt, so every request carried every earlier tool result and every large write argument verbatim.
class_root: The input budget had an owner for the number (laneContextBudget) but no owner for the per-request enforcement: nothing guaranteed that the request actually sent is within the budget.
affected_population: Every Agent turn with several tool calls that return large results (read_script, look_at_canvas, list_models)
Every provider and model (the bound is on our request, not a provider setting)
entry_points: laneHost transform_context: runs before every model request of every turn
pi compaction (between turns) remains the long-term memory mechanism
internal_only_reason: Repository-internal invariants (per-request input size, who classifies a renderer refusal, how long a receipt may stay preparing); the framework only provides the hook point (documented in pi-agent-core types: transformContext / transform_context 'Context window management').
invariants: Every model request's estimated input (system prompt + tool definitions + messages) is within the lane budget unless the irreducible part alone exceeds it
Only old large tool results, then old large call arguments, are dropped from the request view; the latest tool result, latest assistant message and every user message never are
The persisted transcript is never edited; a dropped result says what happened and how to get it back (call the tool again)
generality_proof: The guard runs in the one hook every request of every turn passes through, and its rules depend only on the messages' own sizes, not on tool names or scenarios; the class test feeds a long multi-read turn, write-heavy turns, and an irreducible case.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Every model request of every turn passes the hook; it calls fitContextToBudget with the lane budget and the tool-definition reserve.
pi's between-turn compaction threshold; kept as is, it complements the per-request guard.
The source-side cap on a single tool result; the guard handles accumulation, not one oversized result.

recurrence.reason: Any new tool that returns large results, or any longer conversation, produces the same growth; the registered budget was not binding per request.
same_class_scan: door-map fitContextToBudget / estimateRequestTokens: one call site (laneHost)
pb04 full-walk: 10 requests over budget before, 0 after
the other transform_context consumer (system prompt composition) does not touch messages

prevention.invariant: Per-request estimated input is within the lane budget.
prevention.failure_mode: When the irreducible part alone exceeds the budget the guard reports overBudgetBy and leaves messages intact (fail visible), and the tool-result source cap bounds the latest result.
prevention.strategy: One pure function in the one hook; concept agent-lane.request-input-budget registered; walk invariant 8 (input tokens per request) measures it on a real turn.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The guard is a pure function proven by feeding long turns, write-heavy turns, user-message protection, idempotence and the irreducible case; the real-app proof is the pb04 per-request token measurement.

legacy_paths.rationale: There was no per-request bound before; nothing to remove.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Uses the documented transform_context hook of the installed pi version; no upgrade changes the invariant.

migration: None: only the request view changes; transcripts and settings are untouched.
residual_risks: The size estimate is bytes/3 (conservative for English, close for Chinese); a provider tokenizer can differ.
Images and PDFs in user messages are not elided (user content).

door_reduction.why_not: fitContextToBudget has exactly one caller (laneHost transform_context); estimateRequestTokens is used inside the guard and by its tests.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: The only place that decides what to drop when one model request would exceed the input budget; edits the view of that request only.
